events.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
events.description: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains. Continue reading...
events.ticker_label: 🌪️ California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state

events.title: The U.K. and EU hold a rare summit to strengthen ties
events.description: A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences.

events.title: US judge approves Bayer's $7.25 billion cancer settlement
events.description: Bayer could end years of costly lawsuits in the US over claims that its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer. Tens of thousands of people could now receive compensation, although some lawyers say the payments are too low.

events.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
events.description: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.

events.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
events.description: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

events.title: Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future
events.description: Never before have young people faced so many challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents later in life?

events.title: Can German auto manufacturing recover after Mercedes and VW cuts?
events.description: German automakers are pulling back on investments at home, sparking fresh anxiety about the auto sector's future. Some industry watchers think there is still a narrow window to stem the decline. But how?

events.title: Is Pakistan backing anti-Taliban groups in Afghanistan?
events.description: The Taliban rulers in Afghanistan have accused Pakistan of aiding and sheltering armed resistance groups. The allegations come amid heightened tensions and are likely to deepen the rift between the two neighbors.

events.title: Myanmar genocide ruling: Rohingya say struggle for justice not over
events.description: The ICJ has held Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya and ordered restitution and reparations. Community members have hailed the ruling, but caution that achieving real change will be long and hard.

events.title: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?
events.description: Two challengers to Gianni Infantino have registered for next year's FIFA presidential election. What do Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima stand for – and do they stand a chance against the incumbent?

events.title: Guinea bans Burkina Faso broadcaster, escalating diplomatic tensions
events.description: Tensions rise between Guinea and Burkina Faso after Conakry bans Burkinabe broadcaster RTB, amid a diplomatic dispute over gold miners and a caricature of President Mamadi Doumbouya. Meanwhile, fighting erupts between Congolese forces and the Rwanda-backed FRN group in eastern DR Congo, despite peace commitments. Finally, in Ethiopia, one entrepreneur is tackling period poverty by breaking menstrual stigma and making reusable sanitary pads more accessible.

events.title: A cultural stroll through Paris with singer-songwriters Mariam Doumbia and Zaho

events.title: Trump hails 'fantastic' relationships with China's Xi, Russia's Putin after three-way talks
